summary_en: This study tests whether a lower radiation dose, given with standard chemotherapy, can reduce side effects in people with HPV-positive throat cancer (oropharyngeal cancer). Radiation is given as a total of 30 Gy in 2 Gy fractions over 3 weeks, with cisplatin given by IV at the start of radiation for 2 cycles, and carboplatin and 5-fluorouracil may replace cisplatin. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the study is listed as Phase 2.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si una dosis más baja de radiación, junto con quimioterapia estándar, puede reducir los efectos secundarios en personas con cáncer de garganta asociado al VPH (cáncer de orofaringe). La radiación se administra en una dosis total de 30 Gy, en fracciones de 2 Gy durante 3 semanas, y se da cisplatino por vía intravenosa al inicio de la radiación (2 ciclos); el carboplatino y el 5-fluorouracilo pueden sustituir al cisplatino. El registro no indica una medida principal de resultado; el estudio figura como fase 2.
who_for: HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx, proven by biopsy or surgical tissue.
Measurable disease at the primary tumor site or in lymph nodes.
No distant metastasis on FDG PET/CT.
Age 18 or older, with ECOG 0-2 or KPS 50 or higher.
Hypoxia negative, as stated in the arm descriptions.
not_for: Prior head and neck radiation therapy.
Simultaneous cancers outside the oropharynx (exceptions may be approved).
Prior systemic chemotherapy for this cancer.
Prior invasive cancer, other than non-melanoma skin cancer, without disease-free periods listed.
Severe active conditions, such as recent heart failure, heart attack, serious infection, or COPD flare needing hospital care.
